newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Jews says Nazi gold should go to victims.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Jews says Nazi gold should go to victims.

text.p: Proof in a U.S. report that gold stolen from Holocaust victims was among Nazi stocks meant Holocaust survivors should be given wartime gold still held by the former Allies, Swiss Jews said on Wednesday.

Thomas Lyssy, vice-president of the Swiss Jewish Federation (SIG), said the most important point in the new U.S. government study was proof that Nazi gold stocks included victims' gold as well as loot from occupied countries' central banks.
"I am not surprised. I am happy that we now know this and that it is no longer just speculation," Lyssy told Reuters.

Lyssy said the fact that even a small amount of gold stolen from the Nazis came from death camp victims meant that the rest of the German gold claimed by the United States, Britain and France after the war for occupied countries must now go to individuals.
"The issue now could be the gold still in the U.S. and Britain, the 5.5 tonnes, that Jewish individuals are considered when it comes to distributing this gold," he said.

"I think the report means that responsibility now goes back to the Tripartite Commission," he said, referring to a body set up by the Allies to return looted gold to countries robbed by Hitler's armies.
"This does not mean that Switzerland is absolved of its responsibilities," he added.

Lyssy said Switzerland had already dones a great deal by setting up a historians commission to shed light on its wartime dealings and by setting up a Holocaust memorial fund with 265 million Swiss francs ($181.2 million) from Swiss banks, businesses and the central bank, which bought Nazi gold during the war. ($ = 1.462 Swiss Francs)
